audit_scope: Stage 0 read-only alignment against assets/H-JEPA at the pinned upstream commit

environment.note: nvidia-smi -i 6,7 shows only Xorg (4 MiB) on both cards; GPUs 0-5 untouched.

a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.loading: torch.load(ckpt, map_location='cpu', weights_only=False) then load_training_config_for_checkpoint(ckpt); model.eval(); every parameter requires_grad=False.
a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.num_levels: Read from model.num_levels. fourroom_lewm=1, fourroom_hjepa_l2=2, fourroom_hjepa_l4=4 (training configs num_levels).
a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.dense_encode_no_stride: Level 1: model.get_level(1).encode({'pixels': batch['pixels_level1']}, key='pixels')['embed_0']. Level k>=2: input key f'embed_{k-1}', value = previous level's 'embed_0'; output key is again 'embed_0'. No temporal stride is applied at evaluation (chunk_temporal_inputs is not passed), so every level yields one embedding per input frame.
a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.tensor_keys: Every evaluated level is read from 'embed_0' (shape B,T,D) and flattened to (B*T,D) by _flatten_time. Equivalent to run.py's per-frame embedded[:,0] because a one-frame input gives T=1.
a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.feature_dim: 192 at every level: base fourroom level1.wm.embed_dim=192; l2/l3/l4 level{w}.wm.embed_dim=192. Existing l2 checkpoint reports model.embed_dims == {1:192, 2:192}. L4/LeWM checkpoints are re-verified in Stage 1 after download.
a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.temporal_window_size: Official _validate_dense_assumptions raises unless every level has temporal_window_size == 1. fourroom_hjepa_l2: level1 win=1, level2 win=1 (stride 2 used only for training chunking). fourroom_hjepa_l4 config: every level window_size=1. LeWM is a single JEPA level with the default window_size=1. Checkpoint-level assertion is repeated in run_v2.py.
a_model_loading_and_dense_encoding.loading_result: The same routine generalizes to L=1/2/4 without code changes; only num_levels and the weight path differ.

b_prober_architecture.exact_structure: Linear(input_dim, 512) -> LayerNorm(512) -> GELU -> Linear(512, output_dim). There is exactly ONE hidden layer of width 512, not two.
b_prober_architecture.per_entity_heads: The official loop builds one independent prober per target column. For this wave the two columns are 'xy' (input 2 -> agent_x, agent_y) and 'distractor0_xy' (input 2 -> distractor_x, distractor_y); min_distractor_dist exists in the official defaults but is not used in Wave 1. The two 2-D outputs are concatenated to the 4-D order [agent_x, agent_y, distractor_x, distractor_y].
b_prober_architecture.input_preprocessing: Encoder features are fed raw (no z-score). LayerNorm is applied AFTER the first Linear, on the 512-D hidden activations; it does not normalize the 192-D input.
b_prober_architecture.target_preprocessing: Targets are z-scored with the training normalizer artifact: x_norm = (x - mean) / std per column (h_jepa/data.py L125-L150). The probe loss is MSE in this normalized target space. Physical-unit errors are recovered by multiplying by std (prober_target_std) before NMSE/R2 reporting.
b_prober_architecture.seed: Official probing seed is cfg.seed (fourroom.yaml seed=42) and seeds torch / DataLoader shuffle.

c_official_training_hyperparameters.lr_scheduler: NONE. torch.optim.AdamW is constructed once and stepped every batch for all 60 epochs; no cosine or step decay appears in final_probing_decoding_eval.py.
c_official_training_hyperparameters.dataloader: shuffle=True, drop_last=True, pin_memory=True, num_workers=6 for train; shuffle=False, drop_last=False for eval.
c_official_training_hyperparameters.validation_and_model_selection: There is NO best-checkpoint selection. The eval split is run once per epoch only to log loss; after epoch 60 the CURRENT (final-epoch) prober weights are saved by _save_artifacts. Wave 1 follows this exactly (final-epoch weights), and records the per-epoch val trace for diagnosis.
c_official_training_hyperparameters.official_sample_counts: probing train total_transitions=160000 (levels frameskip=1, num_steps=1 -> per-frame); probing val total_transitions=40000.

d_collection_config_differences.world: IDENTICAL between fourroom_tp35_d1_probing.yaml and fourroom_tp35_d1.yaml: FourRoomDistractors-v0, num_envs=10, max_episode_steps=400, 224x224, agent/distractor speed 2.5, one distractor, teleport_tau=35.
d_collection_config_differences.ego_policy: IDENTICAL YAML values between the probing and non-probing data configs: 50% expert (action_noise=1.0, action_repeat_prob=0.05) + 50% explore.
d_collection_config_differences.run_py_overrides: run.py -- and Wave 1 prepare_data_v2.py -- override exactly four things: seed=<collection_seed>, num_traj=null, num_transitions=400*episodes, ego_policy.mixture.0.params.action_repeat_prob=0.0, plus hydra.run.dir and hydra.job.chdir=false. No other world/policy parameter is changed.
d_collection_config_differences.scientific_difference: The only scientific sampling difference versus the official probing data is action_repeat_prob 0.05 -> 0.0 (already documented in README). Official probing data uses seed=3072 and 600 train / 150 val episodes; Wave 1 deliberately uses new, non-overlapping seeds and larger counts (400 train / 100 val full-frame trajectories).
d_collection_config_differences.num_workers: YAML num_workers=4; run.py does not override it.

e_normalizer_pt_usage.required_by_probing_eval: YES. final_probing_decoding_eval raises FileNotFoundError if normalizer.pt is missing (L608-L618).
e_normalizer_pt_usage.probing_use: Supplies per-column train-set mean/std: (i) z-scores target columns before the probe loss, and (ii) multiplies the de-normalized probe error by std to report NMSE. It does NOT normalize encoder features.
e_normalizer_pt_usage.other_use: Also used by planning / decoding evaluation pipelines; it is not planning-only.
e_normalizer_pt_usage.wave_1_decision: download_extra_weights.py downloads the normalizer.pt belonging to every checkpoint used (9 files, auxiliary) so probe_160k_official uses the official training-set target scaling. This is recorded separately from the 9 checkpoints in assets/setup_v2.json.

checkpoint_verification_stage_1.normalizer_artifact: format/stats/metadata; stats['xy'] and stats['distractor0_xy'] each carry a (1,2) mean and std array; all nine normalizer.pt files share sha256 2bea02d6...f9bf (same training-data transform).
checkpoint_verification_stage_1.conclusion: All 9 checkpoints load as HJEPA objects with the audited level count, 192-D embeddings and window_size=1 at every evaluated level. run_v2.py re-asserts these conditions at load time.

discrepancies_with_expected_prompt_claim: Expected 'two hidden layers of width 512': actual MLP has ONE hidden layer of width 512 (Linear-512 -> LayerNorm -> GELU -> Linear-out).
Expected 'select best weights on val': actual official loop performs NO model selection; it saves final-epoch weights after 60 epochs and uses val only for logging.
Expected 'input features z-score before Linear': actual input is raw; LayerNorm sits after the first Linear on the hidden activations. Only the TARGET coordinates are z-scored (with normalizer.pt).
wave_1_alignment_decision: probe_160k_official is implemented from the audited code, not from the prompt's paraphrase: one hidden layer 512 with LayerNorm+GELU, raw 192-D input, two independent 2-D heads, official normalizer target z-scoring, AdamW(1e-3, 1e-4), batch 128, 60 epochs, drop_last, no scheduler, final-epoch weights.
